Not Impressed
Nov 2019
Location and decor enticed us to look at the menu. The seemingly reasonable prices lured us in. 
Once inside and seated, there was only one brand of beer available even though the menu offered several choices. 
We ordered two dishes (priced at 120,000 & 150,000 vnd each) and asked for a small bowl each so that we could share more easily. 
When the bill arrived we were charged for two dishes at 150,000 each plus two extra charges of 10,000 each. When questioned and prices pointed out on the menu, staff were unable to provide a reason, lacking any ability to speak English. Whilst the ‘extra’ charges are minimal, no one likes being ripped off. 
Food was good, but nothing special or outstanding. 
If sitting on the outside deck area near the street, be prepared for beggars to come up to the edges and ask for money.

Okay but rather disappointing really
Mar 2015 • Family
This property is located on the ground floor of the Saigon Centre building in HCMC.

We selected it as the diners seen through the window all looked happy and seemed to have quite reasonable meals. Sadly, that view was not our experience !

On entering we were told that there were no tables available (free or unbooked) in the air conditioning, and so were led to the outside verandah. Tired and desperate for something to eat, we accepted a table in the shade, only to eventually realise that 30C temperature plus 90%+ humidity was just something one couldn't escape. Our fault for not persevering, and so we suffered during the meal.

We chose Vietnamese dishes; my daughter had "goi cuon" (cold spring rolls) and I wanted "cha gio" (hot spring rolls) as this was the signature dish I had eaten frequently many years before in Vietnam. The goi cuon were rather tasteless according to my daughter (a trained cook) and my cha gio were, in a word ... horrible, with chewy and gristley pork meat filling and still wet from the cooking fat.

I would not recommend this restaurant to anyone unless they were experienced at selecting something "safe" and unlikely to be anything but satisfactory to the palate. Maybe I should have chosen pho soup again !

Prices were low to middle of the range, and drinks likewise. My advice ... NEVER sit outside on the balcony and be careful what you order.

Food, drinks and service were Terrible!
Sep 2014 • Friends
We stumbled upon this place. From outside, it looked decent enough. But were we in for a bad surprise.

First, they seated us at a very small table, cramped along small walking space. We looked around and noticed it was done to many other customers. How were the staff able to move about and serve customers well?

Then the food .... so bad. I had what was supposed to be grilled chicken with rice vermicelli. But the grilled chicken was terrible! Small bits that were definitely not grilled at all.

My friend had the seafood pho, and did not finish his dish. He politely said he was full.

The drinks ... also terrible! Vietnam is supposed to be well known for Vietnamese Coffee. I ordered the Caffe Sua Da but it was so diluted. And the coffee taste was weak. I tasted better Caffe Sua Da at small local coffee houses. Cheaper, too!

I thought of having desserts. Dessert counter might have looked nice. But on closer look, the desserts looked dry, like they have been there for more than 3 days.

And the service ... atrocious! When the waitress who first served us realized we were not Vietnamese, she simply walked away without a word. And then a waiter appeared, who could speak English. No explanation. She just walked away.

And the manager ... needs lots of training. When I did not know to add the sauce and vegetables into the rice vermicelli, he came over and gave instructions to me as if I was a child. And when I started to take some photos (so as to share here on TripAdvisor), he told me off, said no photos allowed. (He could have done it more politely, and quietly so as not to embarrass me in front of other patrons) When I explained I was taking photos to post and share about their cafe on TripAdvisor, he kept quiet. Looked a little shocked, too.

When I return to visit Vietnam, I will Never visit this place again! I highly recommend you don't, too!
